headline: CAMECO HALTS Key Lake Mill — Saskatchewan Flood Severs McArthur River Supply Route
snippet: Cameco halted uranium milling at Key Lake and slowed production at McArthur River — one of the world's largest uranium mines — after a bridge collapse on the Smoothstone River severed the primary supply route into the operations. With slurry tanks holding only 7–10 days of full-production buffer, the timeline for resumption is unknown and could materially affect Cameco's 2026 output guidance.

headline: BARRICK UNLEASHES $3B Buyback as Q1 Earnings Surge 238%, North American Spinoff Advances
snippet: Barrick Gold approved a $3 billion share repurchase program after Q1 2026 earnings surged 238% year-over-year on a realized gold price of $4,823 per ounce, driving record operating margins. The buyback also sets the stage for a planned spinoff of Barrick's premier North American gold assets while the Mali Loulo-Gounkoto complex ramps ahead of schedule.

headline: SILVER SPIKES 7% to $86 as Trump Brands Iran's Peace Offer 'Totally Unacceptable'
snippet: Silver surged as much as 7% to nearly $86 an ounce on May 11 — its highest level in two months — as Trump's rejection of Iran's peace proposal reignited Middle East risk and stoked persistent inflation fears, while gold retreated below $4,700 after giving back last week's $4,720 high. The silver market is now in its sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit.

headline: RECORD HIGH: Copper Tops $6.44/lb as Middle East Acid Shortage Cripples Chilean Refinery Output
snippet: Copper futures surged to an all-time record of $6.44 per pound on May 11 — up 3.1% on the day and 40% year-over-year — as disrupted Middle East sulphuric acid shipments forced Chilean copper refineries to cut heap-leach and anode production capacity, while surging AI datacenter construction drove another wave of demand-side optimism. Southern Copper jumped over 7% on the session.

headline: GALIANO GOLD Drills 32m of 4.7 g/t Au and 53m of 3.9 g/t Au at Ghana's Asanko Mine
snippet: Galiano Gold (TSX/NYSE: GAU) expanded the Abore mineralized system at its Asanko Gold Mine in Ghana with new intercepts well beyond the current underground resource envelope, including 32m of 4.7 g/t Au from 420m depth and 53m of 3.9 g/t Au from 179m. The company has drilled approximately 14,500m of a fully funded 30,000m 2026 program and simultaneously expanded its exploration budget.

headline: ULTRA-HIGH-GRADE: Brixton Drills 13m of 594 g/t Silver — Half-Metre of 7,900 g/t at Ontario's Langis
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSX-V: BBB) reported a standout intercept of 13.0m grading 594 g/t silver — including 0.5m of 7,900 g/t — at the Langis Silver Project in Cobalt, Ontario, one of the strongest results to date from a historically underdrilled area of the former-producer. The company plans to add a second drill in mid-May to accelerate its 60,000m 2026 program toward a maiden resource estimate.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER DELIVERIES Escalate — Are Paper Futures Losing Their Grip on the Physical Market?
snippet: With China acquiring 800 metric tonnes of silver in Q1 2026 alone and physical buyers paying 11% premiums over COMEX spot prices, 24/7 Wall St argues the futures complex is losing pricing authority as the cumulative global silver supply deficit trends toward 866 million oz by year-end. The piece frames escalating physical delivery demands as a structural warning signal for fiat currencies.

headline: Can USA Rare Earth's $2.8B Serra Verde Deal BREAK China's 90% Grip on Rare Earth Refining?
snippet: The Diplomat examines whether USA Rare Earth's $2.8 billion acquisition of Serra Verde Group — the only large-scale producer of all four magnetic rare earths outside Asia — can meaningfully dent China's near-total dominance of rare earth refining. Despite the deal's strategic importance, analysts warn the West will still depend on China for 91% of heavy rare earth demand by 2030, down only modestly from 99% in 2024.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Flips Lithium Outlook: Morgan Stanley Forecasts 80,000-Tonne Deficit in 2026
snippet: A surge in grid-scale battery storage — projected to claim 31% of lithium demand in 2026 versus 23% in 2025 — has turned market consensus from surplus to deficit, with Morgan Stanley forecasting an 80,000-tonne LCE shortfall and Canaccord calling for a 'material market deficit' sustained through the year. The reversal provides a potential re-rating catalyst for lithium juniors battered by two years of oversupply narratives.

headline: Gold Stocks LAGGING the Metal Again — Analyst Sees M&A Window Opening as Cash Flow Surges
snippet: John Feneck tells Kitco that gold equities are significantly underperforming the metal even as producers generate record cash flow at $4,700+ gold, creating a widening valuation gap that historically precedes M&A consolidation — and bargain-hunting by well-capitalised seniors. Feneck names several mid-tier and junior names he believes are acquisition candidates in the current environment.
